endorsements.quote: AI classified as experimental and innovative uses should be required to apply for approval from the relevant research ethics committee (REC).
Following its risk evaluation, an AI system is categorised as minimal‐risk (i.e., standard use ), moderate‐risk (i.e., innovative use ) or high‐risk (i.e., experimental use ).
Similarly, experimental and innovative uses of AI require human‐in‐the‐loop processes to ensure human oversight of the AI's outputs.
Finally, we recommend that additional clinical evidence be collected relative to the AI's risk category.
All risk categories require a process of regular monitoring and iterative review.
In the case of the former, the AI proposal should be offered to patients so that their values and preferences can be considered.
Finally, clinicians will need to make sure that they comply with the relevant regulatory requirements before adopting this tool into clinical practice.

Finally, as an innovative use of AI, Consent‐GPT's performance should be evaluated for its clinical safety and effectiveness via comparative prospective evaluation, such as an RCT or prospective cohort study.

Therefore, Consent‐GPT should be offered as an option (either in addition to, or instead of, typical consent conversations), and patients can choose to validly consent or refuse and interact with a human clinician instead .
Finally (and crucially), implementers should determine whether the risks and expected benefits of implementing an AI system into clinical practice are justifiable (Box 7 ).
Next, implementers should consider potential failure modes, which may be encountered during a system's implementation into clinical practice (Box 4 ).

unlisted_practices: Reject AI systems with no or very weak scientific justification for their intended clinical use until new evidence arises.
Consider whether AI implementation is within cost-effectiveness thresholds and seek alternative funding if it is not.
Seek a wide range of expert opinion, including from different countries and values, when it is unclear whether an AI system's benefits outweigh its risks.
Use deliberative review among the implementing clinical team to weigh AI risks against expected benefits and ensure harms and benefits are fairly distributed.
Involve patients and the public through PPIE focus groups to adjust the assigned values of harms and benefits.
Design standard-use AI with automatic or ongoing self-auditing processes to evaluate outcomes.

screen.reason: This paper presents a conceptual framework and decision algorithm for the ethical and safe implementation/governance of black-box AI and LLMs in healthcare.
